races.name: racingtv.com Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Royal Blaze
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap and cheekpieces fitted; trainer Ewan Whillans has a modest 14-day strike rate, but this 5yo has placed twice at 12f on Standard and handles cut, and at 28 days fresh may find this 1m1f slightly sharp — natural hold-up style could see it racing further forward than usual in a small field.

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Recent form includes a pleasing 2nd on Good ground over 10f; this 6yo is at heart a hold-up horse whose true position is at the rear, though in a six-runner field it will likely end up closer than ideal — headgear (blinkers) suggests it needs caution, and its sole win came over 5f conditions unlikely to apply here.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: confirmed prominent racer for Patrick Morris, and with a 0/9 trainer 14-day record the booking of a 3lb claimer is notable — last two runs produced a second and a fourth at 8f on Standard, and while the step back to soft turf is a query (1/15 in similar going), its control of the pace is the key tactical factor regardless of its finishing position.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie sends this 4yo out just 13 days after its last run, and it carries a ⚠ fade flag consistent with its recent form figures of 9-11-9-8-4; genuinely held-up in style but will occupy a midfield slot by necessity here, and two runs on Soft suggest it handles the ground — though recent evidence of stopping in the finish is a significant concern at this trip.

runners_data.name: Far Ahead
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's 4yo has shown ability with a recent second over 8f on Good and handles soft (placed at 7f/SOF in history); true hold-up runner that will be shuffled into midfield by default rather than choice, and the step up to 9f from recent 8f assignments looks positive for stamina, though 0/14 in similar going is a sobering stat.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo is the youngest and lightest-weighted runner here, and its form of 5-6-7-2-7-6 includes a 2nd over 12f on Standard and a 7th over 10f on Good — hold-up profile, but this trip and surface suit better than recent assignments, and the 15-day freshener with a stable hitting 6/52 at 14 days is at least a neutral angle.

races.paceDynamic: Book Of Life is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press for the lead, can bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on the Good to Soft ground over this 1m1f Hamilton trip. The pace is therefore likely to be honest but not fierce — a single-figure field with one pace-setter rarely produces a truly strong tempo, and on soft ground the fractions could be even more sedate, compressing the race into the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off the pace or attack from a prominent position when the tempo settles, as pure hold-up horses will find themselves on the wrong end of a slow-run contest unless the ground tests stamina severely. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate — Falcon Nine, Storm On Jura, and Far Ahead are all true rear-runners redistributed to midfield, with the horses most likely to actually secure a forward position being Book Of Life on the front end and Royal Blaze or Port Darwin creeping into the first half of the field by default.

watchPoints.text: Book Of Life and Cian Horgan (3lb claimer) — if the leader misjudges the pace on soft ground and goes off too fast, it will have nothing left for Hamilton's punishing uphill finish and the race collapses entirely.

Falcon Nine and Storm On Jura are both genuine hold-up horses racing out of their natural position; watch whether either ends up further forward than expected, as that would fundamentally alter their chance in either direction.

Storm On Jura's repeated fade flag is a concrete concern — if it travels prominently into the straight and then stops, it could cause interference for horses making their run behind it in the closing stages.
Far Ahead's step up to 9f from 8f assignments is worth noting — if the soft ground extends the stamina test, this runner's profile improves meaningfully despite modest recent form figures.

Apprentice/conditional jockeys ride five of the six — watch for positional errors off the break, particularly from Port Darwin (Connor Planas) who may need to dictate where it settles in the early stages given the compressed field size.

races.name: Scullion Law, Law Firm For Life EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qual') (GBB Race)
Follow Us On X @hamiltonparkrc Handicap

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: A consistent course-familiar ten-year-old but the form tag of fading in the finish is damning for a race with a soft, energy-sapping surface; Ben Robinson takes over, the Jim Goldie yard is 9/45 in 14 days, but 0 wins and 0 places from 4 runs at similar going makes this a cold proposition.|

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's five-year-old shows a headline soft-ground effort (3rd at 5f on HEA) and is 2W5P from 12 comparable-going runs — Sam James aboard and an 11-day turnaround all check out, though 14th and 11th in recent starts suggest current form is flat.|

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with headgear (tv) and Good-to-Soft form including a recent second over 5f; the STYLE_FIT flag warns she is running into a positional role that is her natural game yet the 0W1P similar-going record from 2 runs raises doubts about whether soft ground truly suits — David O'Meara's yard in reasonable nick.|

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Dual winner at 5f on soft and good ground, two additional places at the trip, headgear applied (p), and Tim Easterby's yard is a prolific 10/103 over 14 days — this filly lines up in career-best form and her prominent style is a perfect fit for the pace shape Tiva creates.|

runners_data.name: Classy Al
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old Jim Goldie veteran with four consecutive top-four finishes at 5f on good, but the soft-ground record is 0W0P from 5 runs and his true nature as a hold-up horse means he's drawn back into midfield on the map — Amie Waugh claims 3lb but the soft strip looks an issue.|

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' four-year-old owns one win at 5f (Standard) and a recent 5th at the same trip but soft-going placed the 6th, 8th and 15th in comparable conditions on the card; a genuine rear-of-field type whose real position cannot be accommodated in this shape, and the trainer is 0/13 in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners this progressive Jim Goldie four-year-old who has won and finished second on soft/good-to-soft ground at 5f — the 1W3P similar-going figure is encouraging and his headgear (h) indicates he's been set up to race prominently; he has the profile to be dangerous if sitting just off Tiva.|

runners_data.name: Top Juggler
runners_data.note: Dale Spencer's four-year-old won over 6f on good and placed twice on Standard — a natural hold-up horse who is pushed into midfield on the map rather than his preferred deep position; his soft-going effort of 22nd is a significant flag, and the trainer has had just 0/5 runners in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Call Margot
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes the ride on Gemma Tutty's three-year-old, who won over 5f on Standard and placed twice at the trip; she has not raced on soft ground and faces a stiff acid test, though as a hold-up type she could benefit if the pace collapses — the trainer is 0/9 in 14 days.|

races.paceDynamic: Tiva is the confirmed front runner and, with no other natural leader to push her, she should secure an uncontested lead at a sustainable tempo on Good to Soft ground over this sharp Hamilton five furlongs. Canaria Queen is the only other prominent type with genuine early speed claims, and she will likely sit just off Tiva's shoulder, meaning the pace is controlled rather than frantic — a scenario that historically rewards horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort rather than those closing from deep. The field carries a heavy hold-up bias with Jordan Electrics, Solar Aclaim, Call Margot, and the redistributed trio of Top Juggler, Jm Jhingree and Classy Al all natural rear-runners, but the pace map cannot accommodate all of them at the back, and Top Juggler, Jm Jhingree and Classy Al are placed in midfield on the map rather than their preferred rear position. A steady, uncontested gallop set by Tiva strongly favours prominently-raced horses who can travel close to the pace and kick, rather than genuine closers who need a truly run race to generate momentum — Canaria Queen and Montezuma are best placed to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Canaria Queen's soft-ground winning record and front-tracking style make her the most dangerous horse in the field if Tiva's pace proves catchable — watch for Duran Fentiman to stalk Tiva closely throughout and deliver her challenge inside the final furlong.

Tiva's headgear (tv) and 0W1P record at similar going raises the question of whether she can sustain her lead once the soft ground bites in the closing stages — if she ties up, Montezuma and Canaria Queen are poised to pounce.

The redistribution of Top Juggler, Jm Jhingree and Classy Al into midfield on the map means there will be a cluster of horses without their natural position — watch for traffic or crowding issues in the middle of the track at Hamilton, especially entering the final two furlongs.

Montezuma carries headgear (h) and Paul Mulrennan has a strong record from prominent positions — if he settles just behind Canaria Queen rather than behind Tiva, he may be perfectly placed to benefit from any late weakening by the leader.

Jordan Electrics' tendency to fade in the finish combined with the soft surface and a ten-year-old's age means he is worth monitoring as a horse that could block running lanes for closers if he does not quicken when asked inside the final furlong.

races.name: #Cleanstay At Hampton By Hilton Handicap

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on soft ground last time out (1/6f/SOF) and is the most in-form runner here; Tim Easterby's yard is flying (8 wins from 91 in 14 days) and David Allan is a trusted handler of soft-ground sprints, though natural hold-up style means the lack of pace is an equaliser rather than a help

runners_data.name: Catalyse
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner who fades late according to the pace flag, with five consecutive poor runs including a 13th last time; a true hold-up operator pushed into a midfield map slot, and the 0W0P record on similar going (3 runs) makes this a significant ask even if the race falls perfectly

runners_data.name: Annie Edson Taylor
runners_data.note: Won last time at 6f on good ground for Phillip Makin, and the 1W3P similar-going record is respectable, though habitually races further back than ideal; trainer sends only 1 from 5 in 14 days, and the blinkered headgear flag (hg:tb) suggests connections are trying to sharpen her up in a race that will test tactical adaptability

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: At age 8 this mare has twice won over 6f on soft ground (1/6f/SOF in both recent soft runs) and Connor Beasley knows this track well; her similar-going record of 1W3P from 8 tries is the most naturally suited in the field, and she arrives just 7 days fresh with sound fitness

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on soft last time out (1/6f/SOF) for Jim Goldie and arrives 7 days later; the visor (hg:v) has been applied and the 3-pound claim from Amie Waugh aids in a competitive handicap, though a single similar-going run from 15 is a slight concern beyond the most recent evidence

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Finished 4th on soft over 6f most recently and has prior wins at 5f on good ground; the 0W0P record from 3 similar-going runs is a red flag, and stepping back up to 6f from repeated 5f efforts may catch him out in demanding conditions, despite an in-form stable feel

runners_data.name: Emperor's Son
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr takes the ride for the Fahey yard on a horse whose best form is over 5f on standard Tapeta surfaces; the sole similar-going run (4/6f/GOO) and 0W1P record suggest the combination of soft ground and 6f Hamilton is unexplored territory, and a true hold-up runner mapped to midfield further erodes the tactical outlook

runners_data.name: Maldevious
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner returns after the longest absence in the field (29 days) with a 0W1P record from 2 similar-going efforts; consistent mid-pack finishes at 6f on various surfaces hint at a horse who needs luck in running that rarely materialises, and no headgear change signals no obvious stable confidence flag either way

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse with a natural instinct to lead this 6f handicap on soft Hamilton ground. The race will almost certainly begin at a crawl as all eight jockeys look to their rivals to set the fractions, creating a falsely-run, compressed affair that turns into a cavalry charge from the home turn. Stirrup Cup, Pop Star and Iris Dancer are the most recent winners and likely to be produced with the most purposeful forward momentum given the tactical vacuum, but the soft ground will amplify the lottery of a sprint finish. This shape ultimately favours horses with the best late sectional speed and recent form confidence, but with no genuine pace to chase, those who naturally travel into the race off a strong tempo are going to find their trademark weapon removed — the entire field is racing at least partially out of role. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically achieve their ideal position; Stirrup Cup, Iris Dancer and Doon The Glen, all course-distance winners on soft ground, are the likeliest to secure a forward pitch and steal a march in the absence of a true leader.

races.name: Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Sound Janet
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up performer with solid soft-ground form (win and place at similar trips in soft/good-to-soft), though 47 days off the track is a query and her natural rear-of-field role is compromised by the absence of genuine pace to chase.|

runners_data.name: Epidavros
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a string of near-misses and placed form across soft and good-to-soft ground, but consistently on shorter trips than today's mile-and-a-half; the step up in trip could be the making or breaking of her, and her true closing style is squeezed by the lack of pace.|

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner who showed a win two runs ago on good ground over a mile but has no soft-ground evidence at all in five runs; her natural deep hold-up style is already compressed by a field of closers, and the going query adds further risk.|

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer returning from the handicap mark of 65 with tongue-tie, but a run of 0s and 8s in recent form suggests serious decline; still the most likely to go forward and control a slow pace if her rivals are all reluctant to lead.|

runners_data.name: Porth Eilian
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Edward Bethell who landed a win on good ground over a mile last time, stepping up sharply in distance today; Connor Beasley rides and the form string shows consistent progression, making her the most interesting if she travels prominently and the pace is weak.|

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby three-year-old with a win at a mile on good ground and placed efforts at nine furlongs, but soft-ground exposed form is thin; David Allan in the saddle, and a prominent to mid-division position could serve her well in a muddled race.|

runners_data.name: Hot And Cold
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — the only confirmed front-runner in the field, her absence removes the one source of guaranteed early pace and fundamentally changes the race shape, leaving the entire field without a natural leader.|

races.paceDynamic: Hot And Cold is the sole confirmed front-runner here, but is a non-runner, which means this field is left without any genuine pace-setter — the race devolves into a contest where no horse naturally wants to lead. Second Fiddle and Porth Eilian are the most likely to push forward from a prominent position, though neither is a natural front-runner, and the early gallop on Good to Soft ground at Hamilton's flat mile-and-a-half trip is likely to be modest and controlled. Sound Janet, Epidavros, and Geo are all natural hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because there is a surplus of closers in this field — they cannot all obtain their preferred deep position, and whichever of them settles best off a crawl will be best placed. With no genuine pace injection, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or mid-division and produce a sustained run from the two-furlong pole, rewarding hold-up horses only if the pace is truly honest — which, absent Hot And Cold, it almost certainly will not be.

Porth Eilian steps up significantly in trip from a mile to a mile-and-a-half for the first time; if she handles the extra distance, the form uptick and Edward Bethell's yard in form makes her the one to monitor from a prominent pitch.|

races.name: Scottish Racing Supporting #Racingwithpride Handicap

runners_data.name: Beyond The Bar
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on soft, handled the conditions, and this 1m½f trip on today's ground represents a logical stepping-up opportunity for Tim Easterby's 3yo; a genuine hold-up horse who will need the pace to be honest to bring a late run to bear from the rear.

runners_data.name: Whernside
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 3yo has placed twice in good company and Connor Beasley takes the ride; suited to being ridden patiently, though with multiple hold-up types in this field the pace may not be strong enough to draw out a meaningful late challenge.

runners_data.name: Spiritoftheblues
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 3yo goes on good-to-soft and has one win on fast ground, making conditions today broadly acceptable; as the only confirmed pace-setter over 1m½f, David Nolan can control this race from the front, though racing prominently is a style departure from its recent runs and that factor tempers confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Tarmonbarry Kid
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 3yo holds a soft-ground win over 8f and Oisin Orr is a powerful booking at this level; the natural prominent runner who is likely to slot comfortably into second behind Spiritoftheblues, giving him a race-ideal position to challenge off a controlled gallop in the straight.

runners_data.name: Just A Gambler
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo has soft-ground placed form but is a genuine hold-up horse whose true racing style leaves him needing a stronger gallop than this race is likely to produce; Andrew Mullen may find the pace insufficient to bridge the gap from the rear, and the style-fit flag is a legitimate concern here.

runners_data.name: Attention Seeker
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 3yo ran just eight days ago and returns quickly, which is worth monitoring for fitness; a true hold-up operator who, despite today's soft conditions suiting in theory, will struggle to produce a meaningful closing run if Spiritoftheblues engineers a steady, controlled gallop.

races.paceDynamic: Spiritoftheblues is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field over 1m½f on Good To Soft ground at Hamilton, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, David Nolan can set a controlled, uncontested pace from the front. Behind them, Tarmonbarry Kid is the only other natural prominent type, likely to slot into second and keep tabs on the leader without forcing any acceleration. The hold-up contingent — Beyond The Bar, Whernside, Just A Gambler, and Attention Seeker — will be racing from off the pace, but with only one horse dictating a sustainable gallop, the tempo may not be strong enough to suit deep closers on soft ground over this trip. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel within themselves early and quicken on the heels of a controlled leader, rather than pure hold-up horses who need a true pace to close into.

watchPoints.text: Spiritoftheblues holds a structurally dominant role as the sole front-runner — if Nolan dictates entirely unchallenged, monitor whether Tarmonbarry Kid applies any pressure, as a fully uncontested leader on soft ground can be extremely hard to reel in.

Beyond The Bar and Whernside are both genuine hold-up horses whose finishing kicks depend entirely on the pace being true — watch the early splits; if the gallop is slow, both are effectively out of the race before the turn.

Just A Gambler's redistribution to midfield masks a true hold-up profile — Andrew Mullen will not be able to get a natural prominent pitch, and if the pace is slow the horse's chance diminishes sharply from its mapped position.

Attention Seeker returns on just eight days' rest for Brian Ellison — watch the pre-race market moves and the paddock for any signs the quick turnaround has taken a toll, as soft-ground racing over this trip is physically demanding.

Tarmonbarry Kid is the key pace-shape beneficiary — watch whether Oisin Orr elects to sit tight behind Spiritoftheblues or applies pressure early, as the decision at the top of the straight will determine whether the leader is softened up or given a free passage.

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine runner who showed a placed effort (3rd) on heavy ground last time and has soft-going form in the book; Andrew Mullen knows the track well and if Tee Aitch Aye can be placed just off the pace rather than held up, the going and trip are not concerns — recent sim-going record of 1 win from 6 attempts adds modest confidence.

runners_data.name: Galahad Threepwood
runners_data.note: 552-day absence (406 days for jockey David Nolan) is the dominant concern here — no recent racecourse evidence and a long-trip specialist whose best form has come over 17f-21f, well beyond today's 1m3f; a genuine hold-up operator whose position in the race will be dictated by circumstances rather than design, and the layoff alone warrants significant caution.

runners_data.name: Roger Henry
runners_data.note: Lizzie Quinlan runner who carries a hood and has most of his form on standard/AW going — the one soft-ground effort produced a placed finish over 11f, which is mild encouragement; a true hold-up type operating out of his natural position in this pace scenario, and six furlongs shorter than his AW comfort zone adds a genuine distance question mark.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old Jim Goldie veteran with a single placed effort from 15 runs on similar going — limited recent form with a best recent effort of second over 14f on standard; a natural hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map, and the lack of genuine pace makes it hard to see where the winning run comes from for a horse with such a thin similar-going strike rate.

runners_data.name: Uncle Liam
runners_data.note: Four-year-old Jim Goldie runner who has placed three times in five starts, including a win over 12f on good and multiple placings on soft-equivalent going — genuinely stays this trip; a true hold-up type who is mapped to midfield given the volume of similar runners in the field, and a truly-run race would suit far more than the likely steady tempo will allow.

runners_data.name: Stepanov
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this consistent three-year-old who has placed in four of his last five starts including a second on soft and a third on good-to-soft; Edward Bethell yard is active and in form, and Stepanov's ability to sit prominently and produce a finish makes him the most natural beneficiary of a tracking role behind Regulus Black.

runners_data.name: Regulus Black
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground last time out and steps up in trip here; Hugo Palmer in fair recent form (5/25), and Sam James gets a gilt-edged opportunity to dictate on the front end — the absence of pace rivals makes this the race's pivotal tactical asset, though soft ground is untested for this three-year-old.

races.paceDynamic: Regulus Black is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field over 1m3f on soft ground at Hamilton, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Sam James can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without any pressure from rivals. The remainder of the field — Tee Aitch Aye, Stepanov, Galahad Threepwood, Roger Henry, Annandale, and Uncle Liam — are all hold-up or midfield types, meaning the pace ahead of them is unlikely to be truly searching, which tempers the typical late-run advantage those styles rely upon. The field contains more hold-up runners than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Galahad Threepwood, Roger Henry, Annandale, and Uncle Liam are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and in practice Stepanov and Tee Aitch Aye are best-placed to push forward into a tracking position behind Regulus Black. With a lone, uncontested front-runner setting a measured tempo on soft ground over this staying trip, this race shape strongly favours a prominent or tracking profile — a horse that can settle just off Regulus Black and pounce, rather than a genuine hold-up type trying to make up ground from the rear off a steady pace.

watchPoints.text: Regulus Black — if Sam James is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the front, the lack of any pace rival means the race is effectively his to lose before the field even enters the straight.

Stepanov — watch whether Connor Beasley positions him prominently behind Regulus Black rather than dropping him in; if Stepanov tracks the leader, he becomes the most dangerous threat and any drifting back into a hold-up role materially reduces his chance.

Uncle Liam — despite strong placed form and genuine stamina, the slow likely tempo is a specific threat to his hold-up style; watch whether Amie Waugh (3) pushes forward at the start to compensate, which would tell us the yard is aware of the pace scenario.

Galahad Threepwood — the 552-day absence is extreme; watch for any market move or paddock signs of wellbeing, as Ben Pauling's runners fresh can be fit-to-run, but the trip is too short for this horse's optimal range and the layoff makes him a significant unknown.

Going — declared as Good To Soft per the card but the race report lists 5:52 as Good To Soft; confirm any last-minute ground update as the going had been consistent across the card — any genuine softening toward soft would increase the stamina premium and benefit stayers over tactical-speed types.
